name: Inspiaaa/UnityHFSM
description: A fast hierarchical finite state machine library for Unity with zero garbage collection allocations at runtime, coroutine support, and both class-based and lambda-based APIs.
score_rationale: 1.5k stars, zero-GC design makes it well suited for performance-critical game AI in Unity projects.
summary: Fast zero-GC hierarchical FSM library for Unity game AI

name: libgdx/gdx-ai
description: A comprehensive Java game AI framework featuring steering behaviors, formation motion, A* pathfinding, behavior trees, and finite state machines, usable independently of libGDX.
score_rationale: 1.3k stars, covers the full spectrum of classic game AI techniques in a single well-designed Java library.
summary: Comprehensive Java AI framework with trees, pathfinding, steering

name: ricardojmendez/UnitySteer
description: A toolkit for steering, obstacle avoidance, and path-following behaviors for autonomous agents in Unity, reworked from OpenSteer to follow Unity's component-oriented philosophy.
score_rationale: 1.2k stars and well-regarded in the Unity ecosystem for agent steering, though last actively maintained several years ago.
summary: Unity steering behaviors for autonomous agents and NPCs

name: ashblue/fluid-behavior-tree
description: A code-driven behavior tree library for Unity using the builder pattern, with pre-built tasks, a runtime tree visualizer, and TDD-tested implementation for maintainable game AI.
score_rationale: 1.1k stars, emphasizes testability and maintainability with a fluent builder API suited for large Unity projects.
summary: Fluent behavior tree library for Unity with testability focus

name: sploreg/goap
description: A widely-referenced Unity implementation of Goal Oriented Action Planning (GOAP) AI, providing a foundational example of agent-based action planning for game NPCs.
score_rationale: 674 stars and widely cited as a learning reference for GOAP in Unity, though no longer actively maintained.
summary: Learning reference for goal-oriented action planning in Unity

name: stolk/GPGOAP
description: A general-purpose C implementation of Goal Oriented Action Planning (GOAP) that enables NPCs to create robust action plans in a lightweight, engine-agnostic package.
score_rationale: 612 stars, engine-agnostic C implementation of GOAP useful as a foundation or reference for any game platform.
summary: Engine-agnostic C library for goal-oriented action planning

name: linkdd/aitoolkit
description: A header-only C++ library providing finite state machines, behavior trees, utility AI, and GOAP in a single dependency-free package for building NPC brains.
score_rationale: 513 stars, covers four major game AI paradigms in one header-only C++ library with no external dependencies.
summary: Header-only C++ AI library with FSM, trees, GOAP

name: quabug/EntitiesBT
description: A behavior tree framework for Unity's Entity Component System (DOTS) architecture, designed for data-oriented, garbage-free AI execution at scale.
score_rationale: 495 stars, fills a niche for DOTS/ECS-based behavior trees in Unity with zero-GC design.
summary: DOTS behavior tree framework for data-oriented game AI

name: Sollimann/bonsai
description: A Rust behavior tree library for deterministic AI in games and robotics, enabling modular and reactive agent decision-making through composable tree structures.
score_rationale: 440 stars, actively maintained through March 2026, providing a well-designed Rust-native behavior tree option.
summary: Composable Rust behavior tree library for game AI

name: meshula/OpenSteer
description: A C++ library for building steering behaviors for autonomous characters in games and animation, originally developed at Sony with an OpenGL demo application.
score_rationale: 360 stars, the canonical C++ steering behaviors reference library with long history in game AI, though no longer actively maintained.
summary: Canonical C++ steering library by Sony for game characters

name: behavior3/behavior3editor
description: A web-based visual editor for creating and editing behavior trees compatible with Behavior3 libraries, supporting JSON export and multi-tree project management.
score_rationale: 700 stars but last updated in 2015; still useful as a reference visual editor for behavior trees.
summary: Web-based visual behavior tree editor with JSON export

name: MengeCrowdSim/Menge
description: An open-source modular crowd simulation framework in C++ supporting multiple pedestrian behavior models with visualization and extensible plugin architecture.
score_rationale: 151 stars and no longer actively maintained since 2018, but remains a solid reference implementation for game crowd simulation.
summary: Modular crowd simulation framework with behavior models

name: caesuric/mountain-goap
description: A generic C# GOAP library for game AI agents that uses A* pathfinding through action sequences and supports multiple weighted competing goals.
score_rationale: 126 stars, actively maintained with clean composition-over-inheritance design suitable for C# game projects outside Unity.
summary: Generic C# GOAP library with A* pathfinding for AI

name: tildearrow/furnace
description: The biggest multi-system chiptune tracker ever made, supporting over 200 sound chips from classic consoles, computers, and arcade hardware. Compatible with DefleMask modules and supports VGM export.
score_rationale: Industry-leading multi-system chiptune tracker with 3.6k stars, actively maintained, and unmatched in scope of supported hardware.
summary: Industry-leading multi-system chiptune tracker with 200+ chips

name: FluidSynth/fluidsynth
description: A cross-platform real-time software synthesizer based on the SoundFont 2 specification, processing MIDI events to produce audio. Widely used in game engines and music applications across all major platforms.
score_rationale: The de-facto open-source SoundFont/MIDI synthesizer with 2.3k stars, used in countless games and audio applications, actively maintained through 2026.
summary: De-facto SoundFont/MIDI synthesizer used in game audio

name: BleuBleu/FamiStudio
description: A NES/Famicom music editor for chiptune artists and NES homebrewers, featuring a piano-roll interface instead of traditional tracker columns. Supports Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
score_rationale: The premier NES chiptune editor with 1.9k stars, actively maintained through 2025, with broad platform support and a welcoming interface for composers.
summary: Premier NES/Famicom music editor with piano-roll interface

name: steffest/BassoonTracker
description: A browser-based Amiga module tracker in pure JavaScript that plays and edits MOD and FastTracker 2 XM files using WebAudio, with no runtime dependencies.
score_rationale: Unique fully browser-based tracker with 1.1k stars for the classic Amiga module format, actively maintained and accessible without installation.
summary: Browser-based Amiga module tracker for MOD and XM files

name: schellingb/TinySoundFont
description: A SoundFont2 synthesizer library delivered as a single C/C++ header file, enabling easy integration of MIDI/SoundFont audio synthesis into games and applications with zero dependencies.
score_rationale: Elegant single-header SoundFont synthesizer with 793 stars, highly popular for game developers needing lightweight embeddable MIDI playback.
summary: Single-header SoundFont synthesizer for game MIDI playback

name: raysan5/rfxgen
description: A lightweight chiptune-style sound effect generator (fork of sfxr concept) by the raylib author, available as a web tool and standalone executable with command-line batch processing support.
score_rationale: Modern, actively maintained sfxr-style sound effect generator with 498 stars, from the respected raylib ecosystem, updated through 2025.
summary: Modern sfxr-style sound effect generator by raylib author

name: mmontag/chip-player-js
description: A web-based player for dozens of chiptune and video game music formats, built on C/C++ emulation libraries compiled to WebAssembly. Supports NSF, SPC, VGM, MOD, XM, and many more formats.
score_rationale: Comprehensive web chiptune player with 443 stars, actively maintained through 2025, supporting the broadest range of retro game music formats in a browser.
summary: Web chiptune player supporting 50+ retro game music formats

name: davy7125/polyphone
description: A multiplatform open-source SoundFont editor for creating musical instruments, supporting sf2, sf3, sfz, and sfArk formats with a built-in MIDI synthesizer and automatic tuning tools.
score_rationale: The leading open-source SoundFont editor with 452 stars, actively maintained through 2025, filling a niche role in game audio asset creation.
summary: Leading SoundFont editor for game audio asset creation

name: mywave82/opencubicplayer
description: Open Cubic Player is a Unix text-based music visualizer and player supporting over 100 formats including tracker modules, chiptunes, and demoscene formats, with FFT analyzer and oscilloscope displays.
score_rationale: Extensive format-support Unix chiptune player with 407 stars, maintained through 2025 with deep demoscene and tracker music coverage.
summary: Unix tracker music player with 100+ formats and visualizer

name: chr15m/jsfxr
description: A JavaScript port of the classic sfxr retro sound effect generator, available as a web app at sfxr.me and as a Node.js/browser library for generating 8-bit game sounds programmatically.
score_rationale: Popular JavaScript sfxr port with 395 stars, widely used for quick retro sound generation in web games, though not updated since 2021.
summary: JavaScript sfxr port for 8-bit sound generation in games

name: libxmp/libxmp
description: A C library that renders over 90 tracker module formats (MOD, S3M, XM, IT) to PCM audio data, with built-in archive decompressors. The lite version is MIT-licensed and runs on embedded systems.
score_rationale: Essential tracker module playback library with 370 stars, actively maintained through 2026, used by many applications including chip-player-js.
summary: Essential C library for 90+ tracker module formats playback

name: spessasus/SpessaSynth
description: A SoundFont2-based real-time MIDI synthesizer and player written in TypeScript for the browser, with keyboard visualization, Web MIDI API support, and WAV/MIDI export capabilities.
score_rationale: Actively developed TypeScript SoundFont synthesizer with 323 stars and recent 2026 releases, offering a modern web-native MIDI/SoundFont solution.
summary: TypeScript web SoundFont synthesizer with MIDI support

name: libgme/game-music-emu
description: Blargg's video game music emulation library enabling playback of music from NES, SNES, Game Boy, Genesis, TurboGrafx-16, and other classic consoles via a unified C/C++ API.
score_rationale: Foundational retro console music emulation library used by many players and tools, actively maintained through 2025 with broad console format coverage.
summary: Console music emulation library for NES, SNES, Genesis

name: grimfang4/sfxr
description: The original sfxr retro sound effect generator by DrPetter, a seminal tool for creating 8-bit game sound effects that inspired dozens of ports and variants across every major platform and language.
score_rationale: Historically important retro sound generator with 300 stars that spawned an entire ecosystem of ports, though the original C++ codebase is unmaintained.
summary: Original sfxr sound effect generator spawning entire ecosystem

name: sasq64/chipmachine
description: A demoscene and retro music jukebox player supporting over 40 formats including MOD, XM, IT, NSF, SPC, SID, and Game Boy, with incremental search across large music collections.
score_rationale: Broad-format retro music player with 214 stars but last updated in 2019, effectively abandoned though still functional.
summary: Multi-format retro music player with 40+ supported formats

name: inkle/ink
description: inkle's open-source narrative scripting language for writing interactive fiction in games. Supports complex branching, conditions, variables, and integrates with Unity and other engines.
score_rationale: Industry-standard narrative scripting language used in commercial titles like 80 Days, actively maintained, with 4.7k stars and a rich ecosystem of integrations.
summary: Industry-standard narrative scripting language for games

name: nathanhoad/godot_dialogue_manager
description: A powerful, nonlinear, stateless branching dialogue addon for Godot 4 with its own script-like editor and runtime. Widely adopted by Godot game developers for NPC conversations.
score_rationale: The de-facto dialogue manager for Godot 4 with 3.4k stars, actively maintained through 2026, and clean stateless design ideal for complex dialogue trees.
summary: De-facto dialogue manager for Godot 4 with stateless design
